questions.question: What is deflection rate and how do you calculate it?
questions.answer_summary: Deflection rate = (issues successfully resolved by self-service without a human agent) ÷ (total inquiries received) × 100; a team resolving 3,500 of 10,000 inquiries without an agent has a 35% deflection rate.

questions.question: What counts as a 'good' chatbot deflection rate benchmark?
questions.answer_summary: Industry guides put a 'good' deflection rate between 40-60%, with 80%+ considered top tier — though these benchmarks vary by how loosely 'deflected' is defined.

questions.question: Why do some practitioners call deflection rate a 'vanity metric'?
questions.answer_summary: Deflection rate is easy to optimize for and decouples vendor incentives from customer outcomes; one practitioner cited having experienced 65% deflection alongside an 18% increase in customer churn.

questions.question: Is there an industry-standard definition of 'deflection'?
questions.answer_summary: No — some vendors count a ticket deflected if there's no follow-up ticket within 24 hours, others if the customer didn't explicitly ask for a human, others simply if the AI responded at all, regardless of whether the customer engaged.

questions.question: Do vendor-claimed deflection rates match real-world performance?
questions.answer_summary: One vendor (Forethought) has publicly claimed 80-98% deflection in marketing materials, while independent analysis and customer reports put real-world deflection rates in the 44-87% range.

questions.question: What percentage of 'deflected' tickets are actually false deflections?
questions.answer_summary: Cited data shows that while AI deflects more than 45% of queries, only about 14% reach genuine self-service resolution — the other roughly 31% are customers who got a bot response and came back through a different channel.

questions.question: What's the difference between deflection rate and resolution rate?
questions.answer_summary: Deflection rate measures whether a contact avoided a human agent at all; resolution rate measures whether the customer's issue was actually solved, independent of channel — a high deflection rate can coexist with a mediocre resolution rate.

questions.question: How often are 'deflected' tickets actually answered incorrectly?
questions.answer_summary: Audits of RAG-based support deployments cited found 15-25% of 'deflected' tickets were deflected with incorrect or incomplete answers, meaning the customer left without their problem actually solved.

questions.question: Which metric do industry experts increasingly favor — deflection or resolution?
questions.answer_summary: Experts increasingly favor resolution rate because it's closest to the customer's actual experience and ties vendor incentives to real outcomes, unlike deflection rate which just rewards avoiding the human queue.

questions.question: What specific questions should a support leader ask an AI vendor about their deflection numbers?
questions.answer_summary: Recommended vendor questions include: how is deflection specifically defined, what recontact-rate data is available, what verified-resolution numbers do other customers report, and what CSAT gap exists between AI-handled and human-handled interactions.

questions.question: What alternative KPIs are recommended alongside or instead of deflection rate?
questions.answer_summary: Recommended primary KPIs include verified resolution rate (60-75% benchmark) and AI CSAT (4.0+/5), with recontact rate within 72 hours (<15%) and escalation quality score as diagnostic metrics.

questions.question: What is containment rate and how does it differ from deflection and resolution rate?
questions.answer_summary: Containment rate, deflection rate and resolution rate are related but distinct AI-support metrics that are frequently conflated; guides recommend reading all three together rather than reporting just one.
